Foundry · Design review · Pipelines

Three passes at the same page.

The Pipelines page is being replaced. This is every attempt, in the order they happened, each one live and interactive rather than a screenshot. The first two came out of Magic Patterns; the difference between them is one line in the prompt. The third is what is actually running on the branch.

Generated by Magic Patterns from a written brief only. I never sent it the repository — I read two files out of the artifact and hand-translated them.

  • Its own graphite-* Tailwind palette and Inter / JetBrains Mono. Close to Foundry in spirit, but not Foundry’s tokens.
  • Phases carry a role of prepare / build / verify, and a per-phase duration. Neither field exists in PhaseDef. Option B’s columns are built on the invented one.
  • Good instincts on shape — top switcher, grouped canvas, slide-over — which is what actually survived into 03.

Same tool, one difference: the prompt opened with https://github.com/nikships/foundry. It read the repo itself.

  • Every colour is now a real Foundry custom property — var(--bg-void), var(--line-strong), var(--accent-bright) — with Geist, the 3/4/6/8px radii and the 120ms mechanical easing.
  • The data model is the real one: agent | code | engineer, the four-kind Acceptance union, feedbackTo, gates. Its own header comment says “there is no role field”.
  • It pulled the genuine builtin pipelines — Full SDLC and Refine → Build → Ship, with the right phase names. Ship Gate and Docs Refresh it invented; the real builtins contain no checkpoint phase, so it synthesised one.

Written directly against the codebase and running on feat/redesign-pipelines-page. This is the live app code, not a mockup — the same components the desktop build renders, over a seeded in-memory backend.

  • Option A’s gutter draws repair loops as dashed arcs with real geometry; overlapping loops get their own lanes.
  • Option B’s columns are stages derived from your checkpoints, so moving a card across a gate moves the phase past the checkpoint in the ordered array. No schema change.
  • Both are presentations of one usePipelineDraft hook, so auto-save, validation and dry run cannot drift between them. Fully interactive: edit, reorder, add a gate.

The one line that mattered. Passes 01 and 02 are the same tool and the same brief. In 02 the prompt began with the bare repository URL, so Magic Patterns read the codebase itself — which is why its colours resolve to Foundry custom properties and its phase type is the real one. In 01 it had to guess, and invented a role field that Option B was then built on.
